description: While no account exists, anyone can register one with a login and a password and is signed in as its administrator. Once any account exists, registration is closed and answers 403. GET /auth/registration tells whether it is still open.
rationale: The first user sets up the instance without an operator.
title: Register the first account

description: A user signs in with login and password and receives a bearer token, which is also set as an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict session cookie. An unknown login or a wrong password answers 401 without saying which. Logins are compared case-insensitively and surrounding whitespace is ignored.
title: Sign in

description: GET /auth/me returns the signed-in user's login, when the session expires and whether the user is the administrator.
title: Current user

description: POST /auth/logout clears the session cookie and answers 204, signed in or not.
title: Sign out

description: Only the first user, the administrator, lists accounts (login and creation time) and creates new ones; any other user receives 403. Creating a login that already exists answers 409.
title: Administer accounts

description: A login is an email address or a username of letters, digits and . _ % + -, 3 to 254 characters. A password has 8 to 1024 characters. Anything else answers 422 when an account is created.
title: Validate account details

description: Signed-in users list the repositories the GitHub App installation can access and the branches of one of them, a page at a time with the number of the next page.
title: Browse repositories

description: GET /requirements/intake returns the kind question, the kinds of task, the questions asked for each kind and the task question, for the page to show before a session starts.
title: Requirements intake

description: A finalized task is delivered: code is generated or changed, the service and its contract tests are written by separate coding agents, and verification runs the tests against the built service, repairing the failing side a bounded number of times. A bugfix's new tests must first fail against the service as the repository holds it. The session shows the delivery's progress, its agents' questions can be answered, and a failed stage can be retried.
title: Deliver the task

description: Only a delivery that passed verification is pushed, with the repository's updated contract and contract tests, to a new branch of the session's repository. A documentation change, which has no check yet, is pushed and marked as unverified.
title: Publish verified work

description: A user sends a free-form request, optionally with one attached file and a repository to work in, follows it up, retries a failed answer or forks the conversation after one of their messages. Attachments and generated documents can be downloaded.
title: Chat with the LLM

description: Signed-in users list the workflow executions of the namespace, newest first, 50 per page, optionally of one workflow type, continuing with the returned page token.
title: List workflow executions

description: While a requirements session waits for the user, its branch can be checked out again at its latest commit, which the interview reads and the task is finalized against from then on, such as a commit that added the contract the task needs. The session shows the commit it is checked out at. A failed update keeps the earlier checkout and says so.
title: Update a session's checkout

description: Sign-in and registration attempts are limited per client address per minute (AUTH_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS_PER_MINUTE, default 10); further attempts answer 429 with Retry-After.
title: Limit sign-in attempts

description: Passwords, private keys and tokens are never part of a response or a validation error. Passwords are stored as salted scrypt hashes and the GitHub App key is stored encrypted.
title: Never echo secrets

description: Session tokens are HS256 JWTs signed with AUTH_JWT_SECRET (at least 32 characters) that expire after AUTH_TOKEN_TTL_HOURS, 12 by default. Without a usable secret, sign-in and authenticated endpoints answer 503.
title: Expiring sessions

description: When Temporal answers a request with an error or the request storage cannot be reached, an endpoint answers 503 with a detail saying which.
title: Report unavailable dependencies

description: Messages and tasks have at most 10000 characters, an attachment at most 20 MiB and GitHub configuration input at most 16 KiB; larger input answers 413 or 422.
title: Bound request sizes

description: Malformed input answers 422 with a detail; an unknown session or request ID answers 404; an action the session's state does not allow answers 409.
title: Validation errors

description: The backend is a Python 3.12 FastAPI application with Temporal workflows and PostgreSQL storage, in backend/. The web client is a React application in frontend/.
title: Stack

description: Coding agents run in Docker containers built by the workers, without access to Temporal, the database or Docker.
title: Isolated coding agents

description: The Dockerfile at the repository root builds the API as a self-contained service with its own PostgreSQL database, served on port 8080 by a non-root user, so that contract tests can run against it alone.
title: Verifiable service image

description: The delivery pipeline runs a code review step only once both the implementation and the tests exist and verification has shown that they pass against each other.
rationale: User asked for a review step that runs after implementation and tests are ready and verified against each other.
title: Code review step after successful verification

description: The code review step examines only the changes made by the current delivery and reports no findings about code that the delivery did not change.
rationale: User: the step should verify the changes, and only them.
title: Review covers only the delivery's changes

description: The code review step looks for potential issues in the changes that the passing test suite does not cover.
rationale: User: verify the changes for potential issues not covered by tests.
title: Review targets issues the tests do not cover

description: The reviewing LLM's instructions state that not every observation is worth reporting, so that it reports only findings significant enough to need a correction.
rationale: User: the LLM should know that not everything is worth mentioning.
title: Reviewer told not every observation is worth reporting

description: When the code review step reports findings, they are passed as input to the next repair cycle.
rationale: User: findings should be passed to the next cycle.
title: Review findings passed to the next repair cycle

description: Whether the next cycle runs the implementation worker, the test generation worker, or both is decided by the nature of the review findings.
rationale: User: whether the implementation or testing worker runs depends on the nature of the findings.
title: Findings decide which worker runs

description: After a round that corrects review findings, the pipeline runs verification again and, once verification passes, runs the code review step again.
rationale: User chose: verify again, then review again.
title: Verify and review again after fixing findings

description: The number of review-driven correction rounds is capped at 5 by a limit of its own, separate from the existing limit of 5 test repair rounds, and review rounds do not use up test repair rounds.
rationale: User chose a separate limit of review rounds, set to 5 like test repairs.
title: Separate limit of 5 review rounds

description: When review findings remain after the review round limit is reached and the tests pass, the delivery is still pushed to the repository, marked as unverified, and a flag that asks a human for attention is raised in the delivery progress.
rationale: User: push as unverified, raise a flag to the human.
title: Push as unverified when review findings remain

description: When the open-findings flag is raised, the user can either accept the delivery as it is, which clears the flag, or give instructions on what to do about the findings.
rationale: User: ability to tell what to do or accept as is.
title: Human decides on open review findings

description: When a delivery is pushed with open review findings, the commit message of the pushed commit lists those findings.
rationale: User: findings should also be visible in the pushed branch, in the commit message.
title: Open review findings recorded in the commit message

description: For every code review round, the delivery progress shows the findings reported and, for each finding, the worker it was sent to (implementation, test generation, or both). A finding left open that no author of the delivery could settle says why: failing repository tests that no author may change assert otherwise, or the review still found it after its corrections.
rationale: User confirmed: show findings for every review round, with the worker each was sent to.
title: Review findings shown in delivery progress

description: After a delivery's branch has been pushed, the workflow opens a pull request from that branch to the repository's default branch, and the pull request's description says what the delivery changed.
rationale: User: at the end of the workflow, after code is pushed, create a PR to the default branch with a description of what changed.
title: Open a pull request after the push

description: A pull request is opened for every pushed delivery, including unverified ones: documentation changes and deliveries pushed with open review findings.
rationale: User chose: every pushed delivery, including unverified ones.
title: Pull request for every pushed delivery

description: When the pull request cannot be opened because the GitHub App installation lacks the pull request permission, the pushed branch remains, the delivery does not fail, and the delivery progress reports that the permission is missing.
rationale: User chose: report it in the delivery progress without failing the push.
title: Missing pull request permission does not fail the push

description: When a later push goes to a branch that already has an open pull request (after the user's instructions on open review findings), no new pull request is opened; the existing pull request is kept and its description is updated to say what the delivery changed.
rationale: User chose: keep the existing pull request and update its description.
title: Update the existing pull request on a later push

description: A pull request for an unverified delivery is opened as a draft, and when the delivery has open review findings, the pull request's description lists them.
rationale: User chose: draft pull request with the open findings in the description.
title: Unverified deliveries open draft pull requests

description: Once the pull request is opened, the delivery progress shows a link to it.
rationale: User chose: show the pull request link once it is opened.
title: Pull request link in delivery progress

description: When a comment on a pull request mentions the GitHub App and asks for clarification, the app replies in the pull request with an LLM-generated answer based on the delivery's sessions and code.
rationale: User chose an LLM reply in the PR based on the delivery's session and code.
title: Mention the app to ask for clarification

description: The app acts on a mention only when it is on a pull request the app opened for a delivery and its author has write access to the repository; any other mention is ignored.
rationale: User chose: only PRs the app opened, from users with write access.
title: Act only on authorised mentions on the app's PRs

description: Every endpoint other than sign-in, registration, its status, sign-out and POST /connectors/github/events requires a valid, unexpired token, sent as a bearer token or the session cookie, and answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer otherwise.
rationale: Replaces FR-3: GitHub must be able to deliver webhook events without a user token.
title: Require a signed-in user

description: POST /connectors/github/events accepts a GitHub webhook delivery only when its X-Hub-Signature-256 signature matches the connected app's webhook secret, and rejects any unsigned or wrongly signed delivery without acting on it.
rationale: User chose a signed webhook endpoint to receive mentions.
title: Receive GitHub webhook events

description: A mention of the app counts in both pull request conversation comments and inline review comments.
rationale: User chose conversation and inline review comments.
title: Mentions in conversation and inline review comments

description: An LLM classifies each authorised mention as a fix request or a request for clarification; when it cannot tell, the app replies in the pull request asking which one is meant and takes no other action.
rationale: User chose LLM classification with a reply when unsure.
title: Classify a mention as fix or clarification

description: When a fix is requested by a mention while a fix round for the same delivery is running, the request is queued and its round starts after the current round ends, in the order the requests arrived.
rationale: User chose to queue requests that arrive during a running round.
title: Queue fix requests during a running round

description: When a fix round requested by a mention starts, the app replies in the pull request that it has started, and when the round ends it replies again with the outcome: that the result was pushed, or what failed.
rationale: User chose a reply when the round starts and another with the outcome.
title: Acknowledge fix requests in the pull request

description: A GitHub App connection created from an app ID and private key accepts an optional webhook secret, stored encrypted and never returned; while a connection has no webhook secret, POST /connectors/github/events rejects every delivery and mentions are not handled.
rationale: User chose an optional webhook secret entered with the app ID and key.
title: Optional webhook secret for a manual connection

description: All users share one GitHub App connection. It is created from an app ID, its PEM private key, optionally the account it is installed on and optionally a webhook secret, or from the code GitHub returns after creating an app from this instance's manifest. It can be checked against GitHub and removed. Its status shows whether it is configured, whether the key can be encrypted, the app, the installation, when it was last validated and whether a webhook secret is set.
rationale: Replaces FR-8: the user confirmed a manual connection takes an optional webhook secret and the status shows whether one is set.
title: Connect GitHub

description: The delivery progress shows each authorised mention on the delivery's pull request, how it was classified (fix, clarification or unclear) and the fix round or reply it led to.
rationale: User chose to show each mention, its classification and the round or reply it led to.
title: Mentions shown in delivery progress

description: The title and description of the pull request opened or updated at the end of a delivery are written by an LLM from the task, its requirements and the delivery's code diff: the description says what the delivery changed and the purpose of the change, and the title names the specific change instead of a fixed phrase for the task kind.
rationale: User: PR descriptions and titles should describe what changed and why; chose an LLM writing them from the task, requirements and diff.
title: Meaningful pull request title and description

description: The pull request description consists of the LLM-written summary, followed only by the list of open review findings when the delivery has any; it no longer contains the requirement list, the verification status section or the branch and commit details it contains today.
rationale: User chose to replace everything with the new summary, but to keep listing open findings below it (FR-38 stays).
title: Summary replaces the current description sections

description: When the LLM cannot write the pull request title or description (for example, it is unavailable), the pull request is opened or updated with today's generic title and description, and the delivery does not fail.
rationale: User chose a fallback that keeps the delivery from failing.
title: Fall back to the generic title and description

description: The title of a pull request for an unverified delivery carries an "(unverified)" marker in addition to the LLM-written title, as today's generic title does.
rationale: User chose to keep the "(unverified)" marker in the title of draft pull requests.
title: Unverified marker in the pull request title

description: A signed-in user can start onboarding an existing repository as its own action on a chosen repository and branch, outside requirements sessions and the requirements intake.
rationale: User chose a separate action on a repository/branch.
title: Start onboarding from a repository and branch

description: When a contract test fails against the existing code during onboarding, the repair changes the tests (and the drafted contract); the existing code is changed only after the user confirms that the failure reveals a bug in it.
rationale: User chose: the tests, or the code if the user confirms it is a bug.
title: Repair tests, or code only when the user confirms a bug

description: When the chosen branch already has a contract in contracts/, the user is warned before onboarding proceeds and chooses whether to replace it; if the user declines, the onboarding does not proceed and the existing contract is left unchanged.
rationale: User chose: warn and let the user choose whether to replace it.
title: Warn before replacing an existing contract

description: Mentions of the GitHub App on a pull request opened for an onboarding (fix requests and clarifications) are handled the same way as mentions on delivery pull requests.
rationale: User chose: the same as for delivery pull requests.
title: Mentions on onboarding pull requests

description: Onboarding's verification works like a delivery's: test repair rounds and review rounds are each capped at 5, its progress is shown, its agents' questions can be answered and a failed stage can be retried.
rationale: User chose: exactly like a delivery.
title: Onboarding verification and progress like a delivery

description: Signed-in users can list onboardings and reopen any of them to see its state and progress, in the same way as requirements sessions.
rationale: User chose: listed and reopened like sessions.
title: List and reopen onboardings

description: The web client has its own Onboarding tab in the top navigation, where a signed-in user picks a repository and branch and starts an onboarding.
rationale: User chose both a dedicated tab and an entry point from the repository picker.
title: Onboarding tab in the web client

description: The repository picker in the Requirements tab offers an action that starts an onboarding of the selected repository and branch and opens it in the Onboarding tab.
rationale: User chose both a dedicated tab and an entry point from the repository picker.
title: Start onboarding from the repository picker

description: The Onboarding page lets the user do everything the /onboarding/sessions endpoints offer: send messages and answer the interviewer's questions, decide whether to replace an existing contract, update the checkout, finalize, fork after a message, retry a failed turn, follow the delivery progress, answer agent questions (including the confirmation of a bug in the existing code), accept open review findings or give instructions about them, and retry a failed stage.
rationale: User chose: everything the backend offers.
title: Onboarding UI covers every backend action

description: GET /workflows keeps its existing fields (workflow_id, run_id, workflow_type, status, task_queue, parent_workflow_id, start_time, close_time, next_page_token) with their current names and meaning; the change only adds fields.
rationale: User: only add fields.
title: GET /workflows only gains fields

description: For a new service or an API change, an architecture stage runs after the requirements are finished and before the API design, and prepares the task's top-level architecture.
rationale: User: add an architecture stage after requirements, for new service and API change only, before API design.
title: Architecture stage between requirements and API design

description: In the architecture stage an LLM drafts the architecture from the requirements, and the user then reviews and corrects it in a conversation, in the same way as an API design session.
rationale: User chose LLM drafting followed by a review conversation, like API design.
title: LLM drafts the architecture, user reviews it

description: For an API change, when the LLM judges that the task needs no new architecture, it proposes skipping the stage, and the stage is skipped only after the user confirms; a new service always goes through the architecture stage and its skip cannot be proposed or confirmed (confirming a skip for it answers 409).
rationale: User chose: the LLM proposes skipping and the user confirms; skipping is allowed only for an API change.
title: LLM proposes skipping, user confirms (API change only)

description: A new service or an API change continues in an API design session started by its architecture session; the design's conversation records the endpoints, schemas and implementation language, uses the finalized architecture when there is one, and finalizing it renders the OpenAPI document.
rationale: Replaces FR-13: the API design now follows the architecture stage and uses its result.
title: Design the API

description: The finalized architecture document describes the task's components or modules, their responsibilities, the data flow between them and the key technology choices.
rationale: User chose components, responsibilities, data flow and key technology choices.
title: Content of the architecture document

description: The finalized architecture is given to the API design and to the delivery's coding agents, and is committed with the contract as contracts/architecture.md when the delivery is pushed. When an API change skips the stage, the repository's existing contracts/architecture.md is kept unchanged and is the architecture given to the API design and coding agents.
rationale: User chose: fed to API design and coding agents, committed to contracts/; a skipped API change keeps the existing architecture.md.
title: Architecture used downstream and committed

description: Architecture sessions are served under /architecture/sessions with the same actions as API design sessions (get the session, send a message, answer the interviewer's questions, retry a failed turn, finalize, fork after a message and download the document) plus an action that confirms the proposed skip of the stage.
rationale: User chose endpoints like API design plus a skip confirmation.
title: Architecture session endpoints

description: Forking an architecture session whose API design has already started answers 409.
rationale: User chose: forking is not allowed once the API design has started.
title: No fork once the API design has started

description: Each OnboardingWorkflow, RequirementsWorkflow, ArchitectureWorkflow, ApiDesignWorkflow and DeliveryWorkflow execution returned by GET /workflows includes the repository and branch it works in, and the Flows page shows them.
rationale: Replaces FR-71: user chose to treat the architecture workflow like API design.
title: Repository and branch in GET /workflows

description: The Flows page offers an Architecture filter that lists only ArchitectureWorkflow executions.
rationale: User chose to offer the architecture workflow as a filter.
title: Architecture filter on the Flows page

description: Onboarding produces for the repository the full contract in contracts/ (requirements.json, requirements.md, api.json, openapi.yaml, language.json and architecture.md, the architecture drafted by an LLM from the existing code), contract tests and a root Dockerfile, and the contract tests are verified to pass against the existing code built with that Dockerfile.
rationale: Replaces FR-57: user chose that onboarding drafts contracts/architecture.md, which is now required.
title: Onboarding produces the full contract, tests and Dockerfile

description: For an API change, the architecture session drafts its architecture starting from the repository's existing contracts/architecture.md, and the finalized architecture replaces that file when the delivery is pushed.
rationale: User chose: start from the existing one and replace it with the finalized result.
title: API change starts from the existing architecture

description: An LLM drafts the requirements, the architecture and the API from the repository's existing code, and the user reviews and corrects all three drafts in the same interview before the onboarding is finalized.
rationale: Replaces FR-58: user chose that the drafted architecture is reviewed in the same onboarding interview.
title: LLM drafts the contract, user reviews it

description: When the chosen branch already has a contract in contracts/ but no contracts/architecture.md, onboarding offers, in addition to replacing the whole contract or not proceeding, to add only architecture.md; choosing it drafts and adds contracts/architecture.md and leaves every other file of the existing contract unchanged.
rationale: User chose: onboarding offers to add only architecture.md for repositories whose contract predates this change.
title: Onboarding adds only a missing architecture

description: When the user declines the LLM's proposal to skip the architecture stage, the proposal is dismissed, the stage is not skipped, and the conversation continues with the user explaining what the architecture should cover.
rationale: User chose: the proposal is dismissed and the user explains what the architecture should cover.
title: Declining a skip proposal

description: When onboarding adds only contracts/architecture.md, an LLM drafts it from the existing code, the user reviews and corrects it in the onboarding interview, and it is then pushed to a new branch with a pull request to the repository's default branch, without contract tests, verification or code review.
rationale: User chose: draft, review in the interview, push with a pull request; no tests, verification or code review.
title: Architecture-only onboarding is reviewed and published without tests

description: The result of an onboarding that produces the full contract goes through the code review step and is pushed to a new branch with a pull request to the repository's default branch, in the same way as a delivery; an onboarding that adds only contracts/architecture.md is pushed and gets a pull request without code review.
rationale: Replaces FR-60: the user chose no code review for architecture-only onboarding.
title: Publish onboarding like a delivery

description: The code review step runs for new service, API change and bugfix deliveries and for onboardings that produce the full contract, and does not run for documentation-only deliveries or for onboardings that add only contracts/architecture.md.
rationale: Replaces FR-62: the user chose no code review for architecture-only onboarding.
title: Review applies to code-producing deliveries and full onboarding

description: Today, after a delivery has pushed its branch and its pull request has been merged, the delivery (and the requirements session it belongs to) is still shown as running on the Flows page, because the finished delivery keeps waiting for a user decision or a pull request mention for up to 14 days (TASK_IDLE_TIMEOUT) and nothing reacts to the merge.
rationale: User: a feature pipeline was finished, pushed, merged and deployed, but is still shown as running. Code: DeliveryWorkflow waits after the push; webhooks only handle comment events.
title: Problem: flow stays running after its pull request is merged

description: When a delivery's pull request is merged, the delivery stops waiting and completes, and the flow it belongs to (its requirements, architecture and API design sessions) completes too, so none of them is shown as running on the Flows page.
rationale: User chose: the delivery closes and its whole flow completes.
title: Merged pull request completes the whole flow

description: When a delivery's pull request is closed without being merged, the delivery and its whole flow stop and are shown on the Flows page as cancelled (abandoned), not as running or completed.
rationale: User chose: the flow closes and is shown as abandoned/cancelled.
title: Pull request closed without merging cancels the flow

description: The app learns that a delivery's pull request was merged or closed from GitHub pull_request webhook events, and, while the delivery waits after its push, also checks the pull request's state periodically, at an interval that is configurable and defaults to one hour, so the flow closes even when no webhook arrives (for example, when the connection has no webhook secret).
rationale: User chose both: webhook with a periodic check as a fallback; interval configurable, default every hour.
title: Detect merge or close by webhook, with a periodic check as fallback

description: After a delivery's pull request is merged, the delivery and its requirements, architecture and API design sessions are shown as completed on the Flows page no later than one check interval after the merge, even when no webhook event arrives.
rationale: User's acceptance criterion.
title: Acceptance: merged pull request shows the flow as completed

description: A delivery that was already waiting after its push when the fix is deployed also completes, together with its flow, once its pull request is merged (and is cancelled once it is closed without merging).
rationale: User's acceptance criterion: existing waiting deliveries must close too.
title: Acceptance: deliveries already waiting also close

description: When an onboarding's pull request is merged, the onboarding stops waiting and is shown as completed on the Flows page; when it is closed without being merged, the onboarding is shown as cancelled; both are detected in the same way as for a delivery's pull request.
rationale: User chose: onboardings behave the same as deliveries.
title: Onboardings close when their pull request is merged or closed

description: When a comment on a pull request mentions the GitHub App and asks for a fix, the comment's text is passed to a new round of fixes, followed by verification and code review; while the pull request is open, the result is pushed to the pull request's branch, as with the user's instructions on open review findings.
rationale: Replaces FR-40: the user confirmed that a fix is pushed to the pull request's branch only while the pull request is open.
title: Mention the app to request a fix

description: When a delivery's or onboarding's pull request is merged or closed while its open-review-findings flag is still raised, the flow still completes or is cancelled. On the Flows page it is shown as completed or cancelled with an "unresolved findings" marker, and it is not highlighted as waiting for the user.
rationale: User chose: the flow closes and the flag stays visible as unresolved. A closed flow gets a marker only and is not highlighted as waiting.
title: Open review findings stay visible after the flow closes

description: Forking a requirements, architecture or API design session whose flow has completed or been cancelled answers 409.
rationale: User chose: forking any session of a closed flow answers 409.
title: No fork of a session of a closed flow

description: When the user gives instructions about open review findings, the instructions are passed to a new round of fixes, followed by verification and code review; while the delivery's pull request is open, the result is pushed to the same branch as the unverified delivery.
rationale: Replaces FR-31: the user confirmed the same branch is used only while the pull request is open (closed flows: FR-111).
title: Human instructions start a new fix round on the same branch while the PR is open

description: A requirements session starts in a chosen repository and branch from the intake: the kind of task (new service, API change, bugfix or documentation), the answers to that kind's questions and what needs to be done. An LLM interviewer then records requirements while the user sends messages or answers its questions. A failed turn can be retried, and a session can be forked after any message while its flow has not completed or been cancelled.
rationale: Replaces FR-10: the user confirmed forking works only while the session's flow is not closed (FR-112).
title: Specify a task in a requirements session

description: The web client shows every flow on one Flows page instead of separate Chat, Requirements, API design, Onboarding and Workflows tabs. The page lists the top-level flows; opening one lists its child flows and steps with their statuses, highlights each one of a flow that has not completed or been cancelled that is waiting for the user (unanswered questions, a coding agent's questions, open review findings or a contract decision) with a button that opens its questions, shows a completed or cancelled flow with open review findings only with an "unresolved findings" marker, and opens a flow's conversation, session or onboarding in a panel on the same page. New chats, requirements interviews and onboardings are started from that page.
rationale: Replaces FR-75: the user confirmed closed flows are not highlighted as waiting, only marked (FR-110).
title: One page for every flow

description: When a delivery or onboarding is pushed but no pull request can be opened (for example, because the pull request permission is missing), the delivery or onboarding and its whole flow complete right after the push instead of waiting until TASK_IDLE_TIMEOUT.
rationale: User chose: complete right after the push, since there is no pull request to wait for.
title: Flow without a pull request completes after the push

description: The GitHub App manifest this instance offers requests the pull_requests: write permission in addition to its existing permissions, turns on the webhook pointing at POST /connectors/github/events, and subscribes to pull request conversation comment, inline review comment and pull request events; the webhook secret GitHub returns with the created app is stored encrypted with the connection.
rationale: Replaces TR-5: the user confirmed the manifest also subscribes to pull request events so merges and closes are seen.
title: Pull request permission, comment and pull request webhooks in the app manifest

description: When an LLM's message text, question or question option mentions a requirement ID (for example FR-12, NFR-3 or TR-1), the web client marks the ID, and hovering over it with the mouse or tapping it shows that requirement's text.
rationale: User: a user should see the requirement text on mouse hover/finger tap; IDs recognised in the message text, the questions and their options.
title: Show requirement text on hover or tap

description: A mentioned ID is resolved against the requirements recorded in the session, the existing service's requirements and the requirements retired by the task, so the text of any of them is shown.
rationale: User chose all of them.
title: Which requirements can be looked up

description: The responses of GET for requirements, architecture, API design and onboarding sessions include a new field listing every requirement a mentioned ID can refer to (recorded in the session, the existing service's and those retired by the task), each with its ID, title, description, priority, category and whether it is retired.
rationale: User chose a new field in each session response.
title: Lookup requirements in session responses

description: The text shown on hover or tap for a requirement ID gives its ID, title, description, priority and category, and is marked "retired" when the task retires that requirement.
rationale: User chose ID, title, description, priority and category with a retired marker.
title: Content of the requirement popup

description: A requirement-ID-like text (such as FR-999) that matches no known requirement is still marked, and hovering over or tapping it shows "Unknown requirement".
rationale: User chose to mark unknown IDs and show "Unknown requirement".
title: Unknown requirement IDs

description: Requirement IDs are recognised in any letter case and with or without the dash (for example FR-12, fr-12, FR12 and fr12), and each form is looked up as the same requirement (FR-12).
rationale: User chose to also recognise lowercase forms and forms without the dash.
title: Recognised forms of requirement IDs

description: A published bugfix commit's subject names the specific change rather than "Fix the service and add regression tests", and its LLM-written subject is at most 72 characters; with the LLM unavailable, the push succeeds and the commit has today's fixed subject.
rationale: User's acceptance criteria, including the 72-character subject check.
title: Acceptance: descriptive, bounded subject with a working fallback

description: When docker() is cancelled or its timeout expires while the docker process is still running, it first sends SIGTERM, waits up to 10 seconds for the process to exit, and sends SIGKILL only if the process is still running after those 10 seconds.
rationale: User chose SIGTERM first, then SIGKILL after 10 seconds.
title: docker() terminates gracefully before killing

description: docker()'s wait for the process it terminated or killed is shielded from a further cancellation, so that even when the calling task is cancelled again during that wait, the docker process has exited and been reaped before the cancellation propagates.
rationale: User chose to make the reap safe against a second cancellation.
title: docker() always reaps the stopped process

description: A test runs docker() with a fake docker that ignores SIGTERM and writes its PID atomically, cancels the call, and shows that the call raises CancelledError, the fake is killed after the 10-second grace period, and os.kill(pid, 0) then raises ProcessLookupError.
rationale: User's acceptance criterion.
title: Acceptance: a process ignoring SIGTERM is still killed and reaped

description: A test cancels a running docker() call, cancels it again while docker() waits for the stopped process, and shows that once the CancelledError reaches the caller, os.kill(pid, 0) for the fake docker's PID raises ProcessLookupError.
rationale: User's acceptance criterion.
title: Acceptance: a second cancellation during the reap leaves no running process
